trail.text: Memory and latency spikes point to orders — I'll trace the failure across callers.
Orders shows the strongest deviation — now checking other services to separate the origin from downstream effects.
Early signs narrow the field — now pinning down onset timing to confirm the source.
Error onset in orders precedes the rest — now verifying propagation and filling out the remaining candidates.
Orders' abrupt memory jump confirms it as the epicenter — now gathering final evidence on downstream impact.

causes.reasoning: Orders memory tripled from ~321MB to ~930MB with sharp jump at +13s plus memory failures and first errors at +10s, indicating a leak/OOM pressure originating here.
Front-end p99 latency spiked 0.10s to 0.86s starting at +14s right after orders errors, consistent with a caller blocked by orders.
Catalogue p99 latency spiked at +29s after orders degradation, showing downstream tail-latency victim effect with no memory/CPU anomaly of its own.
User p95 latency rose later at +38s with small magnitude, consistent with secondary congestion from the orders incident.
Payment shows only mild memory rise exceeding at +115s much later, indicating weak sympathetic effect rather than origin.
